Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average free memory as the scaling metric.

explanation:
The correct choices enable dynamic scaling of both compute and storage to handle rising load. A) RDS storage Auto Scaling increases storage automatically when needed, preventing the Oracle DB from running out of space as traffic grows. D) Using average CPU as the ASG scaling metric allows adding instances in response to higher compute demand, matching the increasing workload.
B) Migrating to Aurora is not necessary for Auto Scaling storage and adds migration risk; not the asked solution. C) Low free storage alarm is reactive, not automatic scaling. E) Free memory is not a reliable ASG metric for EC2 auto scaling in this context; CPU is the standard scaling signal.

question:
A company provides an online service for posting video content and transcoding it for use by any mobile platform. The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so that multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing. As the popularity of the service has grown over time, the storage costs have become too expensive.
Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

choices.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway for files to store and process the video content.
Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.
Use Amazon EFS for storing the video content. Once processing is complete, transfer the files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.

explanation: Amazon S3 is the most cost-effective scalable storage for infrequently accessed or variable video content, with lifecycle policies and tiering (e.g., S3 Standard-IA, Glacier) reducing ongoing costs while still allowing high-throughput access for processing. Processing directly from S3 avoids the cost and complexity of EFS or EBS for large, shared datasets. A) Storage Gateway file interface adds on-premises illusion and latency, not cost savings. B) Gateway for volumes is for block storage on-premises, not ideal for shared EC2 access. C) EFS is already in use and not as cost-efficient for long-term storage. D) Moving data to EBS adds per-volume costs and does not optimize storage economics.

question:
A company wants to create an application to store employee data in a hierarchical structured relationship. The company needs a minimum-latency response to high-traffic queries for the employee data and must protect any sensitive data. The company also needs to receive monthly email messages if any financial information is present in the employee data.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use Amazon Redshift to store the employee data in hierarchies. Unload the data to Amazon S3 every month.
Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the employee data in hierarchies. Export the data to Amazon S3 every month.
Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly events to AWS Lambda.
Use Amazon Athena to analyze the employee data in Amazon S3. Integrate Athena with Amazon QuickSight to publish analysis dashboards and share the dashboards with users.
Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly notifications through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) subscription.

explanation:
B) E)
B correctly uses DynamoDB for low-latency, high-traffic hierarchical data access and exports monthly to S3 for durable storage/analysis, aligning with the need for fast responses and data protection via managed AWS services. E uses Macie for data discovery/classification and EventBridge to trigger monthly notifications, delivering the required monthly alerts about sensitive financial information via SNS.
A is incorrect because Redshift is for analytic workloads with higher latency and involves ETL to S3, not optimal for low-latency hierarchical lookups. C is incorrect because Macie alerts are classifications, not a direct monthly financial-notification mechanism via EventBridge + SNS. D is incorrect because Athena/QuickSight provide analytics, not the specified alerting for sensitive data.

question:
A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.

Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.

explanation:
A) AWS Backup can manage DynamoDB backups with a monthly schedule, apply a lifecycle to move to a cheaper storage class after 6 months, and set a retention period of 7 years, meeting all three requirements in a centralized, compliant manner.
B) DynamoDB on-demand backups do not natively support automated lifecycle transitions to S3 Glacier or a 7-year retention policy; separate steps would be required, making it less automated and not aligned with built-in lifecycle features.
C) Custom scripts with EventBridge introduce operational complexity and potential gaps; lifecycle transitions and long-term retention are not as reliably enforced as with a managed AWS Backup plan.
D) AWS CLI + EventBridge without built-in retention policy does not provide centralized lifecycle management; transitions and deletions would rely on ad-hoc scripting, risking non-compliance.

question:
A company is using Amazon CloudFront with its website. The company has enabled logging on the CloudFront distribution, and logs are saved in one of the company’s Amazon S3 buckets. The company needs to perform advanced analyses on the logs and build visualizations.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.

explanation:
Athena supports SQL queries directly over data stored in S3, including CloudFront access logs, and QuickSight provides visualizations from Athena query results, making B the correct choice.
A incorrect: Visualizing Athena results with AWS Glue is not a visualization service; Glue is for ETL/cataloging, not dashboards.
C incorrect: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and does not natively query data in S3; CloudFront logs in S3 require Athena, not DynamoDB.
D incorrect: DynamoDB for analysis is unsuitable; CloudFront logs reside in S3 and must be queried with Athena, with QuickSight for visualization.

question:
A company runs a fleet of web servers using an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. After a routine compliance check, the company sets a standard that requires a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 1 second for all its production databases.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
Enable auto scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone.
Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and create multiple read replicas in a separate Availability Zone.
Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) tasks.

explanation:
Multi-AZ deployment provides synchronous replication to a standby in a different AZ, ensuring near-zero RPO in case of failure, meeting <1 second requirement.
A) Correct. Multi-AZ for RDS PostgreSQL achieves synchronous replication to a standby AZ, enabling immediate failover with minimal RPO.
B) Auto scaling for a single AZ DB is not a real feature for RDS; scaling does not address RPO and fails to provide a standby in another AZ for high availability.
C) Standby in another AZ via read replicas introduces eventual consistency; replicas are asynchronous and do not fulfill <1 second RPO on failover.
D) DMS CDC tasks are for migration/continuous replication to other targets, not for RDS high availability or automated failover within the same DB instance.

question:
A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VPC. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across the public subnets directs web traffic to the EC2 instances. The company wants to implement new security measures to restrict inbound traffic from the ALB to the EC2 instances while preventing access from any other source inside or outside the private subnet of the EC2 instances.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Configure a route in a route table to direct traffic from the internet to the private IP addresses of the EC2 instances.
Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow traffic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
Move the EC2 instances into the public subnet. Give the EC2 instances a set of Elastic IP addresses.
Configure the security group for the ALB to allow any TCP traffic on any port.

explanation:
The correct answer is B.
- B) By restricting the EC2 instances' security group to only allow inbound traffic from the ALB’s security group, you ensure that only ALB-originated traffic can reach the instances, effectively isolating them from all other sources inside and outside the VPC.
- A) Incorrect: Routes to private IPs from the internet would expose EC2 instances; no direct internet access is needed or desired in a private subnet.
- C) Incorrect: Moving to public subnets and assigning Elastic IPs exposes instances to the internet and undermines private-subnet security.
- D) Incorrect: Allowing all TCP traffic from the ALB’s security group is unnecessarily permissive; it should be restricted to the necessary ports (e.g., 80/443) and validated by the instance’s own SG.

question:
A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application. The simulation application runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes. The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system.
The company maintains two synchronized file systems. This strategy is causing data duplication and inefficient resource usage. The company needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon FSx File Gateway for storage.

Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to exchange data between the applications.
Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.

explanation:
The correct answer is D. FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a scalable, fully managed SMB file system suitable for Windows applications and can be mounted by Windows EC2 instances, enabling seamless data sharing with the Linux-based simulation via NFS-compatible workflows through NFS/SMB cross-compatibility as needed, without code changes.
A is incorrect because Lambda cannot host persistent SMB/NFS workloads or long-running simulations; data exchange via S3 would require application changes or additional glue, not preserving existing file-sharing behavior.
B is incorrect because FSx File Gateway is for backing on-premises or hybrid file shares, not native cross-OS SMB/NFS access between EC2 Linux and Windows without code changes.
C is incorrect because SQS is a messaging service, not a shared file system, so data exchange would require redesign of the data store and is not transparent to both apps.

question:
As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets. A solutions architect needs to determine the most efficient way to obtain this report information.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
Access the bill details from the billing dashboard and download the bill.
Modify a cost budget in AWS Budgets to alert with Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).

explanation:
A concise, accurate explanation:
B) Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report. Cost Explorer provides itemized or grouped cost and usage data by linked account or user, suitable for department budgeting, and supports downloadable reports. It is designed for cost visibility and report generation.
A) Athena requires data export and schema setup; not the most efficient for per-user itemized reports.
C) Billing dashboard access is limited in scope and not designed for automated, exportable per-user reports.
D) AWS Budgets alerts do not generate itemized reports by user and are for thresholds, not reporting.

question:
A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

Create a t2.micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

explanation:
A) The dynamic form would require managing containers and SES integration; ECS adds unnecessary orchestration for low traffic.
B) Correct: API Gateway with a Lambda backend is serverless, cost-effective for under 100 visits/month, and can securely invoke SES to send emails without provisioning servers.
C) Lightsail with client-side form still not ideal for dynamic server-side processing; WorkMail is for hosted mailboxes, not email-sending from forms, and this adds unnecessary complexity.
D) EC2 with LAMP is overprovisioned for light traffic, incurs server management overhead, and WorkMail integration is not suited for form-to-email workflows.

question:
A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not reflect updates that have been made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments.
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Add an Application Load Balancer.
Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website’s SSL certificate.

explanation:
The correct answer is C. Invalidate the CloudFront cache to ensure updated S3 content is served to end users, forcing CloudFront to fetch the latest objects from S3 after deployment.
A) Adding an Application Load Balancer does not address caching or content updates for a static site served from S3 via CloudFront.
B) ElastiCache in the database tier does not affect static asset delivery or CloudFront caching behavior.
D) ACM only manages SSL/TLS certificates; it has no role in propagating updated static content through CloudFront.

question:
A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers.
How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.

Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.

explanation:
Hosting all three tiers on EC2 with FSx for Windows File Server provides native SQL Server features (backups) on the database layer and seamless Windows-compatible file sharing across tiers.
A) FSx File Gateway is for on-premises to cloud access, not optimal for in-cloud Windows file sharing and native SQL Server features.
C) RDS for SQL Server supports backups but file sharing across tiers via EFS is not Windows-native and RDS limits cross-tier file sharing.
D) io2 EBS volumes are block storage, not suitable for shared file access across multiple instances natively and do not support SQL Server native backups as a shared file system.

question:
A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.

explanation: The correct answer is C. Amazon EFS provides a managed, scalable, POSIX-compliant file system that can be mounted by multiple Linux instances concurrently, enabling shared file access without modifying the application. A) S3 is object storage, not a shared filesystem, and wouldn’t present a POSIX mount expected by the app. B) CloudFront is a CDN for caching/accelerating web content, not a shared file system. D) EBS gp3 volumes cannot be mounted on multiple instances simultaneously; EBS is block storage for a single instance, not a shared file system.

question:
A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?

choices.text: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.

explanation:
The correct approach uses an IAM role assumed by the Lambda function with a scoped policy granting read access to the specific S3 bucket, providing least privilege and secure credential handling.
A) Insufficient: a bucket policy can grant access but does not tie to the Lambda execution role and may be broader than necessary.
C) Embedding keys in code is insecure; Lambda should use roles, not hard-coded credentials.
D) Grants read access to all buckets in the account; violates least privilege by broad scope.
B) Correct: role-based access with a scoped bucket policy ensures secure, least-privilege access for the Lambda function.

question:
A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand. The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long-term commitment.
Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Dedicated Instances only
On-Demand Instances only
A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances

explanation:
A) On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances provide the best balance of flexibility and cost savings for variable workloads without long-term commitments.
B) On-Demand alone does not maximize savings when demand fluctuates; costs are higher than using Spot when capacity is available.
C) Correct: mix of On-Demand and Spot allows scaling with demand, using cheaper Spot capacity for variable, interruptible workloads, while On-Demand preserves baseline availability in an Auto Scaling group.
D) Reserved Instances require long-term commitment and are less suitable for dynamic scaling and uncertain traffic; they’re not optimal for a non-committed, fluctuating workload.

question:
A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. The company wants to secure the video content that is hosted in Amazon S3 by controlling who has access. Some of the company’s users are using a custom HTTP client that does not support cookies. Some of the company’s users are unable to change the hardcoded URLs that they are using for access.
Which services or methods will meet these requirements with the LEAST impact to the users? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Signed cookies
Signed URLs
AWS AppSync
JSON Web Token (JWT)
AWS Secrets Manager

explanation: Signed URLs and signed cookies provide time-limited access control for CloudFront delivered S3 content. Signed URLs work with clients that cannot handle cookies by embedding access parameters in the URL, while signed cookies protect requests from browsers or clients that do support cookies, enabling access control without changing hardcoded URLs. AWS AppSync is for API GraphQL/real-time data and not suitable for direct S3/CloudFront access control. JSON Web Token (JWT) is a token concept but not an AWS-native mechanism for CloudFront signed requests; it would require additional verification logic. AWS Secrets Manager stores credentials, not access control for delivery.

question:
A company is preparing a new data platform that will ingest real-time streaming data from multiple sources. The company needs to transform the data before writing the data to Amazon S3. The company needs the ability to use SQL to query the transformed data.
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data. Use Amazon EMR to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

explanation:
A) Reason: Kinesis Data Streams for ingestion, Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL-based transformation, Kinesis Data Firehose to S3 delivery, and Athena to query S3 data aligns streaming ingest, in-stream transformation with SQL, durable S3 storage, and serverless SQL querying.
B) Reason: MSK for streaming, Glue for ETL and S3 load, and Athena for SQL queries on S3 meets real-time ingestion via MSK, batch/ETL transformation with Glue, and SQL access via Athena.
C) Incorrect: DMS is for migrations, not real-time streaming; EMR is heavier Hadoop/Spark-based; querying via Athena is fine only after S3, but flow isn’t optimal for streaming SQL transformation.
D) Incorrect: RDS query editor cannot query data in S3; using MSK with Kinesis Data Analytics plus RDS editor is not standard or supported for S3-based querying.
E) Incorrect: Uses RDS query editor for S3 data and combines Kinesis Data Streams with Glue but Firehose is redundant; not aligning with SQL query path on S3.

question:
A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.

Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

explanation:
Amazon Storage Gateway with a stored volume gateway maintains data on-premises and asynchronously backs up a copy to AWS, ensuring local access to all data while securely transferring backups to the cloud.
A) Snowball migrates data and provides a new endpoint; it does not support on-premises mounted access to actively backed-up data.
B) Snowball Edge offers on-device storage and file interface, but Snowball Edge is not the standard solution for continuous backed-up access with on-premises mount points.
C) Cached gateway stores a subset locally; not all data remains on-premises, so immediate local access to the entire dataset isn’t guaranteed.
D) Stored volume gateway maps gateway volumes to on-premises storage, keeping data on-site for local access while backing up to AWS.

question:
An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet.
How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.

explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 ensures that S3 traffic from the VPC remains on the AWS network and does not traverse the Internet. This is the correct mechanism to meet the requirement.
A) Private hosted zone via Route 53 is for internal DNS resolution, not for ensuring private network paths to S3.
C) NAT gateway would route traffic to the Internet for instances without public IPs, not ideal for S3 and still incurs egress via the Internet.
D) Site-to-Site VPN connects networks, not directly to S3; it would add complexity and is unnecessary for S3 access within AWS.

question:
An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use the data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications process the data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.
Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.
Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon S3 buckets so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective S3 bucket.
Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.

explanation:
The correct choice is B because S3 Object Lambda can transform data on-the-fly to remove PII before the other two apps access it, minimizing data duplication and operational overhead while centralizing control over data masking.
A is incorrect because a proxy layer increases complexity, adds maintenance burden, and does not inherently guarantee consistent PII removal across apps.
C is incorrect due to data duplication across three buckets, increasing storage, synchronization, and governance overhead.
D is incorrect for similar reasons to C and because DynamoDB is not ideal for large terabytes-scale data with multiple analytic access patterns and masking needs.

question:
A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC.
What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?
explanation: A) 10.0.1.0/32 is too small for a VPC CIDR block; a VPC requires a non-hosted CIDR range that supports at least two IPs per subnet and the VPC itself must have a valid size. B) 192.168.0.0/24 overlaps entirely with the development VPC’s CIDR, which is not allowed for VPC peering. C) 192.168.1.0/32 is a single IP, not a valid VPC CIDR. D) 10.0.1.0/24 provides a non-overlapping, valid CIDR block suitable for VPC peering with 192.168.0.0/24 and satisfies size requirements.

question:
A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%.
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.

Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization matric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.

explanation:
Deploying an Auto Scaling group with target tracking on CPUUtilization ensures automatic, cost-effective scaling in response to traffic surges, while maintaining a minimum and maximum instance count and using the existing ALB and target group. B is correct because it uses target tracking with a sensible target value (50%), provides scalable capacity (min 2, max 6, desired 3), and leverages the ALB for load distribution.
A is incorrect because terminating instances based on low CPU is destabilizing and not a typical scaling pattern; it can reduce capacity during demand.
C is incorrect because it lacks a dynamic scaling policy, risking insufficient capacity during spikes.
D is incorrect because relying on manual SNS notifications without automated scaling fails to meet the automation and cost-optimization requirements.

question:
A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance.
The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone.
Which solution will make the application highly available?

choices.text: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.

Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

explanation:
A subnet per AZ, and Multi-AZ DB deployment ensures EC2ASG spans both AZs and RDS provides synchronous replication across AZs for failover. Option C matches: subnet in each AZ, ASG distributes across AZs, RDS Multi-AZ for high availability.
A) Incorrect: “DB instance with connections to each network” is vague and not a standard HA design; Cross-AZ DB sync requires Multi-AZ, not arbitrary connections.
B) Incorrect: Subnets “extend across both AZs” are not valid; subnets must reside in a single AZ.
D) Incorrect: Subnet across both AZs is not valid; also only one subnet cannot be in multiple AZs, and Multi-AZ DB deployment paired with properly segmented per-AZ subnets is required.

question:
A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data.
Which solution will meet the performance requirements?

choices.text: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Sat each volume’ tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the fila system on the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

explanation:
The correct answer is B.
A) FSx for NetApp ONTAP with ALL tiering cannot provide the combined sub-millisecond latency and 6 GBps for hundreds of Linux EC2s; ONTAP typically adds latency and complexity for Lustre-style HPC workloads.
B) FSx for Lustre with SSD storage and S3 import/export delivers high-throughput (often 6 GBps+ with SSD) and sub-millisecond metadata/latency for parallel EC2 access, ideal for HPC-style processing with data in S3.
C) HDD-based FSx Lustre lowers throughput and increases latency, failing the 6 GBps requirement.
D) FSx for NetApp ONTAP with NONE tiering also risks higher latency and does not match Lustre’s HPC throughput profile for large data sets.

question:
A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.

explanation: The most cost-effective, scalable approach is to use EC2 Reserved Instances for the steady-state, always-on application and Aurora with Reserved Instances for the growing relational database, providing billed capacity savings and managed, auto-scaling-friendly storage with high performance. A) Spot Instances are not suitable for 24/7 production due to interruption risk; S3 is not a direct relational storage replacement for a growing DB. B) RDS On-Demand is more expensive for continuous use, and RDS on-demand with EC2 RI mismatches persistence needs. D) On-Demand EC2 increases costs; RDS Reserved Instances are not compatible with Aurora (Aurora uses its own reservation model).

question:
A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share.
The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must take place within the next 5 days.
Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: AWS Snowcone
Amazon FSx File Gateway
AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family

explanation:
AWS DataSync is designed for fast, automated data transfer between on-premises storage and AWS services, including FSx for Windows File Server, with built-in bandwidth throttling to control impact on other networks and accelerated transfer performance suitable for large datasets like 30 TB within tight windows.
A) AWS Snowcone is a small, portable edge device for offline data transfer, not suited for high-volume online migration with bandwidth control over a shared link.
B) Amazon FSx File Gateway is for cached on-premises access to FSx in the cloud, not optimized for large, full-mesh migrations with strict bandwidth throttling.
D) AWS Transfer Family is for SFTP/FTPS/FTP access to S3, not designed for direct FSx migration and bandwidth management in this scenario.

question:
A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app captures video clips and uploads the video clips in raw format into an Amazon S3 bucket. The app retrieves these video clips directly from the S3 bucket. However, the videos are large in their raw format.
Users are experiencing issues with buffering and playback on mobile devices. The company wants to implement solutions to maximize the performance and scalability of the app while minimizing operational overhead.
Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching.
Use AWS DataSync to replicate the video files across AWS Regions in other S3 buckets.
Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances in Local Zones for content delivery and caching.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.

explanation: Choose two. CloudFront caches and delivers the videos from edge locations close to mobile users (less buffering, scales automatically). Elastic Transcoder (now superseded by AWS Elemental MediaConvert) converts the large raw clips into mobile-friendly formats with no servers to manage. DataSync replication, EC2 fleets in Local Zones, or EC2 transcoding fleets all add operational overhead.

question:
A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high traffic to the application upon its launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases.
What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.
Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.

explanation:
Using AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies allows ECS Fargate services to scale in response to utilization metrics (CPU/memory) and automatically adjust desired count to maintain a target value, reducing costs during low utilization without manual intervention.
A) Incorrect: EC2 Auto Scaling applies to EC2 instances, not Fargate tasks; cannot manage ECS service scaling for Fargate.
B) Incorrect: Lambda reacting to CloudWatch alarms is a more complex, less scalable pattern for ECS service scaling and not designed for native service auto scaling.
C) Incorrect: Simple scaling policies via EC2 Auto Scaling are for EC2 instances, not for ECS/Fargate services; not appropriate for Fargate.
D) Correct: Application Auto Scaling supports ECS services with target-tracking policies and integrates with CloudWatch metrics to maintain target utilization.

question:
A company recently created a disaster recovery site in a different AWS Region. The company needs to transfer large amounts of data back and forth between NFS file systems in the two Regions on a periodic basis.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Use AWS DataSync.
Use AWS Snowball devices.
Set up an SFTP server on Amazon EC2.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).

explanation:
The correct answer is A) Use AWS DataSync. DataSync is purpose-built for high-performance, automated data transfer between on-premises storage or NFS file systems across regions with minimal operational overhead, including scheduling, incrementals, and secure transfers. It supports large-scale transfers and ongoing synchronization, ideal for DR scenarios requiring periodic data movement.
B) Snowball is a physical device for bulk transfers, not suitable for ongoing periodic synchronization with low overhead. C) EC2 SFTP adds management overhead and is not optimized for large-scale, automated NFS-to-NFS data transfer. D) DMS is for database migrations, not file-system or NFS data replication.

question:
A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.
Which AWS solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.

explanation:
A short, fully managed SMB-compatible shared storage solution is provided by FSx for Windows File Server, which delivers Windows-native file shares (SMB) with automatic management and scalability. Therefore option C is correct.
A) DataSync is for data transfer/replication, not for hosting a persistent SMB file share in a fully managed service.
B) EC2 Windows with a self-managed file share requires manual maintenance and is not a managed service.
D) S3 is object storage with no native SMB mount; mounting to SMB clients is not supported natively and requires extra layers.

question:
A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes more than 100,000 transactions each minute and requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost-effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
Launch all EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with partition strategy when launching EC2 instances.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones based on a network utilization target.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.

explanation:
Launching all EC2 instances in the same AZ within the same region and using a cluster placement group concentrates low-latency, high-throughput inter-instance networking, reducing cross-AZ data transfer and network latency for an in-memory, latency-sensitive workload.
A) Correct. Cluster placement group keeps instances physically close, lowering network latency and data transfer costs for in-memory workloads.
B) Wrong. Partition strategy across AZs introduces more inter-AZ traffic and higher latency/costs, degrading performance for a cache-like in-memory DB.
C) Wrong. Auto Scaling across AZs improves availability but may increase cross-AZ data transfer and latency; placement strategy not addressed.
D) Wrong. Step scaling across AZs focuses on throughput targets but does not optimize inter-instance bandwidth or placement for latency-sensitive memory workloads.

question:
A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises. The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally.
Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Amazon S3 File Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes

explanation:
Caching with Volume Gateway cached volumes keeps most data in AWS while retaining recently accessed data locally, reducing on-premises iSCSI storage growth and minimizing local scaling. It meets the requirement to keep only recently accessed data locally while migrating from on-prem to AWS.
A) S3 File Gateway primarily provides object storage access via NFS/SMB and is not optimized for iSCSI and on-premises block storage caching.
B) Tape Gateway emulates tape libraries for archival, not suitable for active recently accessed data caching.
C) Stored volumes keep all data on-premises and syncs to AWS, not minimizing local storage as requested.
D) Cached volumes specifically cache hot data in local storage and tier the rest to AWS.

question:
A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days. The company’s finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts.
The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS. The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs.
Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.
Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.

explanation: With consolidated billing, the payer (consolidated billing) account sees Trusted Advisor checks across all member accounts at once. The DB instances are active On-Demand instances that have run for 90 days, so the check that reduces cost is Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization. The Idle DB Instances check doesn't apply to busy instances, and the Redshift check is for a different service.

question:
A solutions architect needs to optimize storage costs. The solutions architect must identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed.
Which solution will accomplish this goal with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 dashboard in the AWS Management Console.
Turn on the Amazon CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric for buckets. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the metrics data with Amazon Athena.
Turn on AWS CloudTrail for S3 object monitoring. Analyze bucket access patterns by using CloudTrail logs that are integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

explanation:
S) A) S3 Storage Lens provides comprehensive, automated usage and access patterns across all buckets with minimal setup, enabling identification of rarely accessed or unused buckets at scale.
B) S3 dashboard alone offers basic metrics and lacks the breadth of Storage Lens insights needed for efficient, low-effort optimization.
C) CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes shows size, not access frequency, and using Athena adds manual querying overhead.
D) CloudTrail logs track API activity but require substantial processing and correlation to infer access patterns, increasing operal overhead.

question:
A company sells datasets to customers who do research in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The datasets are large, formatted files that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company hosts a web application that the customers use to purchase access to a given dataset. The web application is deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. After a purchase is made, customers receive an S3 signed URL that allows access to the files.
The customers are distributed across North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce the cost that is associated with data transfers and wants to maintain or improve performance.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing S3 bucket. Direct customer requests to the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.
Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.

Set up a second S3 bucket in the eu-central-1 Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Direct customer requests to the closest Region. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.

Modify the web application to enable streaming of the datasets to end users. Configure the web application to read the data from the existing S3 bucket. Implement access control directly in the application.

explanation: CloudFront delivers content from an edge network close to users, reducing latency and egress costs for global customers while keeping S3 as the origin and using signed URLs (or signed cookies) for secure access. A) S3 Transfer Acceleration is region-specific and increases cost with unclear latency benefits for global users; not ideal for fine-grained access control. C) Cross-region replication adds cost and complexity; it doesn’t improve latency for direct authenticated access to signed URLs. D) Streaming via app-level access removes direct S3 access control and is not advantageous for large datasets and signed URL-based authentication. B is the correct approach for global performance with secure access.

question:
A company is using AWS to design a web application that will process insurance quotes. Users will request quotes from the application. Quotes must be separated by quote type, must be responded to within 24 hours, and must not get lost. The solution must maximize operational efficiency and must minimize maintenance.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Create multiple Amazon Kinesis data streams based on the quote type. Configure the web application to send messages to the proper data stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to use the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to pool messages from its own data stream.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each quote type. Subscribe the Lambda function to its associated SNS topic. Configure the application to publish requests for quotes to the appropriate SNS topic.

Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.

Create multiple Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams based on the quote type to deliver data streams to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Configure the application to send messages to the proper delivery stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly.

explanation:
C) Using a single SNS topic with per-quote-type SQS queues via message filtering ensures reliable, decoupled processing with strong delivery guarantees (SQS queues at-least-once, decoupled consumers, scalable via fan-out). Filters route only relevant messages to each queue, and each backend server processes its own queue, minimizing maintenance and maximizing operational efficiency.
A) Kinesis streams and KCL adds complexity and per-type streams; not as cost-efficient for simple request/queue processing and maintenance growth.
B) SNS with Lambda per type introduces function-per-type scaling, potential cold starts, and stricter execution limits; not as resilient as queue-based decoupling.
D) OpenSearch-based delivery is unnecessary for processing quotes and adds unnecessary search infrastructure and maintenance.

question:
A company has an application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances. Each EC2 instance has multiple Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) data volumes attached to it. The application’s EC2 instance configuration and data need to be backed up nightly. The application also needs to be recoverable in a different AWS Region.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.text: Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application’s EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Region.
Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EC2 instances as resources.
Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EBS volumes as resources.
Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application's EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Availability Zone.

explanation:
AWS Backup provides centralized, automated nightly backups of EC2 (via EBS volumes) and can copy backups to another region, satisfying both instance configuration/data backup and cross-region recoverability with minimal operational overhead. It supports tagging and resource-based backup plans, simplifying management across multiple volumes and instances.
A) Lambda-based nightly EBS snapshots require custom orchestration and don’t inherently manage cross-region backup or multi-resource scope as cleanly.
C) Similar to B but specifies only EBS volumes; misses potential recovery of instance config and requires more manual mapping for full restoration.
D) Copying to another Availability Zone does not offer cross-region recovery, which is required.

question:
A company is building a mobile app on AWS. The company wants to expand its reach to millions of users. The company needs to build a platform so that authorized users can watch the company’s content on their mobile devices.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.
Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.

explanation:
A short summary: Using Amazon CloudFront with signed URLs best meets scalable, authorized mobile content delivery.
A) Not correct: Public S3 content lacks access control; signed URLs via CloudFront are standard for authorized access.
B) Not correct: IPsec VPN between mobile app and AWS is unnecessary for streaming scale and adds overhead; not ideal for wide-end-user access.
C) Correct: CloudFront edge caching with signed URLs authenticates requests and enables scalable, low-latency delivery to millions of devices.
D) Not correct: AWS Client VPN is for private access to VPC from devices, not optimized for large-scale content streaming delivery.

question:
A company has an on-premises MySQL database used by the global sales team with infrequent access patterns. The sales team requires the database to have minimal downtime. A database administrator wants to migrate this database to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of more users in the future.
Which service should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Amazon Aurora MySQL
Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
Amazon Redshift Spectrum
Amazon RDS for MySQL

explanation:
Aurora Serverless for MySQL (B) provides a scalable, on-demand capacity model with minimal downtime and automatic scaling, which fits infrequent access and future user growth without choosing a fixed instance type.
A) Amazon Aurora MySQL is a managed continuous provisioned cluster; it would require selecting instance types and may incur more downtime during scaling rather than serverless automation.
C) Amazon Redshift Spectrum is for querying data lakes with Redshift, not a relational OLTP database migration target.
D) Amazon RDS for MySQL requires fixed provisioned instances and manual scaling, not the serverless, on-demand capability.

question:
A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers. The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Deploy AWS Shield to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Create an AWS Lambda function to log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Deploy Amazon Macie and AWS Lambda functions to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Turn on Amazon GuardDuty. Deploy the GuardDuty agents to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.

explanation:
Amazon Inspector is the dedicated service for automated security assessments of EC2 instances, with agents installed on the instances and findings reported to AWS, which can be automated into reports via Lambda. This matches the requirement to actively scan EC2 instances and generate detailed findings reports.
A) AWS Shield protects against DDoS, not vulnerability scans; it does not perform host-level vulnerability assessment or reporting.
B) Amazon Macie is for data discovery and classification, not vulnerability scanning; it does not scan EC2 hosts or produce vulnerability reports.
C) GuardDuty analyzes for threats but does not perform active vulnerability scanning of EC2 hosts; reporting via Lambda is not its primary workflow.
D) Correct: Inspector agents perform ongoing vulnerability assessments; Lambda can automate reporting.

question:
A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining its ability to process a growing number of messages that are added to the queue.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.
Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.
Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.

explanation:
A) The correct answer is C.
C) Migrating the poll/processing script to AWS Lambda with appropriate runtime enables event-driven, on-demand processing and automatic scaling with SQS. Lambda scales out with concurrent invocations as message volume grows, reducing idle costs compared to a constantly running EC2 instance.
A) Increasing EC2 size increases costs and does not address automatic scaling or cost efficiency for growing message volumes.
B) EventBridge alone cannot orchestrate or optimize continuous message processing cost-effectively; it is not a direct substitute for polling/processing workloads.
D) Run Command executes on-demand administrative tasks, not a persistent, scalable message-processing solution.

question:
A company uses a legacy application to produce data in CSV format. The legacy application stores the output data in Amazon S3. The company is deploying a new commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) application that can perform complex SQL queries to analyze data that is stored in Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3 only. However, the COTS application cannot process the .csv files that the legacy application produces.
The company cannot update the legacy application to produce data in another format. The company needs to implement a solution so that the COTS application can use the data that the legacy application produces.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
Develop a Python script that runs on Amazon EC2 instances to convert the .csv files to .sql files. Invoke the Python script on a cron schedule to store the output files in Amazon S3.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use an S3 event to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in the DynamoDB table.

Use Amazon EventBridge to launch an Amazon EMR cluster on a weekly schedule. Configure the EMR cluster to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in an Amazon Redshift table.

explanation:
The correct answer is A because an AWS Glue ETL job provides serverless, scheduled data processing to transform CSVs and load into Redshift, enabling the COTS SQL queries with minimal maintenance and operational overhead.
B is incorrect due to added EC2 management, scripting, and ongoing maintenance for scheduling and reliability, increasing overhead compared with serverless Glue.
C is incorrect because DynamoDB is not a suitable target for SQL-based analytics required by the COTS tool, and Lambda-based ETL introduces state and concurrency challenges for large CSVs.
D is incorrect as EMR clusters on a weekly schedule add significant operational overhead and slower iteration compared with a managed Glue ETL workflow.

question:
A company recently migrated its entire IT environment to the AWS Cloud. The company discovers that users are provisioning oversized Amazon EC2 instances and modifying security group rules without using the appropriate change control process. A solutions architect must devise a strategy to track and audit these inventory and configuration changes.
Which actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing.
Use data lifecycle policies for the Amazon EC2 instances.
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and reference the security dashboard.
Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
Restore previous resource configurations with an AWS CloudFormation template.

explanation:
A) Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing. CloudTrail records API activity, enabling tracking of who provisioned oversized EC2 instances and who modified security groups, satisfying audit requirements.
D) Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes. AWS Config continuously monitors resource configurations and changes, and Config Rules enforce governance and compliance over inventory and configuration drift.
B) Data lifecycle policies apply to data aging but not auditing or inventory tracking. C) Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks, not detailed per-resource change auditing. E) CloudFormation templates can capture configurations but do not provide ongoing change auditing or real-time drift tracking.

question:
A company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 Linux-based instances in the AWS Cloud. Systems administrators have used shared SSH keys to manage the instances. After a recent audit, the company’s security team is mandating the removal of all shared keys. A solutions architect must design a solution that provides secure access to the EC2 instances.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?

choices.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.
Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.

explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager eliminates the need for SSH keys by providing secure, auditable, browser or CLI-based access to instances without opening inbound ports. This reduces administrative overhead since you don’t manage keys, bastions, or long-lived credentials.
A) Correct: Session Manager provides secure, centralized access with IAM controls and logging.
B) Incorrect: AWS STS one-time SSH keys would still require key management and distribution; adds overhead.
C) Incorrect: Bastions reintroduce shared access and key management complexity; increases surface area.
D) Incorrect: Cognito/Lambda for SSH key generation adds custom infrastructure and monitoring burden; not least overhead.

question:
A company is using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest data from on-premises data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is rebooted, the data in-flight is lost. The company’s data science team wants to query ingested data in near-real time.
Which solution provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?

choices.text: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.
Store ingested data in an EC2 instance store. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
Store ingested data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Publish data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data.

explanation:
K) A) is correct because Kinesis Data Streams provides durable, real-time data ingestion with minimal loss on rebots, and Kinesis Data Analytics can query streaming data with near-real-time results, meeting scalability and latency needs for JSON data at up to 1 MB/s.
B) Firehose is near-real-time but typically stores to Redshift with batch-like loads; Redshift is not optimized for low-latency streaming queries, leading to higher latency and potential data loss during retries.
C) EC2 instance store is ephemeral and not durable; S3/Athena are batch-oriented, not suitable for near-real-time queries or minimal data loss on instance reboot.
D) ElastiCache is in-memory cache, not a durable streaming ingestion or querying layer; Redis pub/sub does not provide scalable, durable streaming analytics or near-real-time query capability for continuous ingestion.

question: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?

choices.text: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.

explanation:
S) D is correct because enforcing server-side encryption via an S3 bucket policy ensures all uploaded objects are encrypted at rest using SSE (e.g., AES-256 or AWS KMS). The policy denies PutObject requests lacking the x-amz-server-side-encryption header, guaranteeing encryption regardless of client behavior.
A and B are incorrect because ACL handling does not guarantee encryption; they control access and object visibility, not encryption at rest. C is incorrect because enforcing secure transport (HTTPS) ensures in-transit security, not at-rest encryption of objects. Therefore, only D directly enforces SSE for all uploads.

question:
A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. The application's users upload images from a mobile device. The application generates a thumbnail of each image and returns a message to the user to confirm that the image was uploaded successfully.
The thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to provide a faster response time to its users to notify them that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application to asynchronously dispatch requests to the different application tiers.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.
Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.

Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.

explanation:
S) C) creates an asynchronous, durable decoupled workflow: images enqueue as messages, allowing thumbnail processing to occur independently while immediately informing the user that the image was received. SQS provides a reliable queue with at-least-once delivery and works well for decoupling the upload, processing, and notification steps.
A) Incorrect: custom Lambda alone would couple processing to the user notification and may not scale or decouple reliably; 60-second processing could slow responses for user confirmation.
B) Incorrect: Step Functions adds orchestration but is heavier for a simple queue-based decoupling; it isn’t as inherently asynchronous with durable queues as SQS.
D) Incorrect: SNS topics with push notifications require additional processing to ensure thumbnail generation is complete before notifying the user; not as clean for decoupling the workflow.

question:
A company’s facility has badge readers at every entrance throughout the building. When badges are scanned, the readers send a message over HTTPS to indicate who attempted to access that particular entrance.
A solutions architect must design a system to process these messages from the sensors. The solution must be highly available, and the results must be made available for the company’s security team to analyze.
Which system architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

choices.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as the HTTPS endpoint and to process the messages. Configure the EC2 instance to save the results to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Create an HTTPS endpoint in Amazon API Gateway. Configure the API Gateway endpoint to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
Use Amazon Route 53 to direct incoming sensor messages to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection from the facility network to the VPC so that sensor data can be written directly to an S3 bucket by way of the VPC endpoint.

explanation:
