The recommended serverless architecture with API Gateway invoking Lambda provides a scalable, highly available HTTPS endpoint for badge readers and durable storage in DynamoDB for fast queryable results, meeting HA and analysis needs without managing servers.
A) EC2 endpoint introduces operational burden, potential single point of failure, and slower scale compared to Lambda for event-driven bursts.
C) Route 53 is a DNS service, not an HTTP endpoint or event-driven processor; cannot directly process sensor payloads.
D) VPC gateway endpoint to S3 with Site-to-Site VPN adds complexity and latency; S3 is for object storage, not for structured, queryable analysis and real-time processing.

question:
A company wants to implement a disaster recovery plan for its primary on-premises file storage volume. The file storage volume is mounted from an Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) device on a local storage server. The file storage volume holds hundreds of terabytes (TB) of data.
The company wants to ensure that end users retain immediate access to all file types from the on-premises systems without experiencing latency.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the company's existing infrastructure?

choices.text: Provision an Amazon S3 File Gateway as a virtual machine (VM) that is hosted on premises. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Modify existing applications to access the files through the NFS protocol. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and mount the S3 bucket that contains the files.

Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Use a data backup solution to back up all existing data to a virtual tape library. Configure the data backup solution to run nightly after the initial backup is complete. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and restore the data to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from the volumes in the virtual tape library.

Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volume. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Mount the Volume Gateway cached volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.

Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volume with the same amount of disk space as the existing file storage volume. Mount the Volume Gateway stored volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.

explanation:
A) The S3 File Gateway with VM cache would introduce latency for active on-prem users and requires changing access through NFS; it also relies on cloud egress for recovery, which violates “immediate access” requirement.
B) Tape gateway is for archival backups, not for active file serving with low latency, and recovery involves restore from tape—not suitable for immediate access.
C) Cached volume gateway reduces cloud reliance but still requires initial copy of all data to the gateway cache and relies on snapshot restores, which adds risk for immediate access during disaster.
D) Volume Gateway stored volume preserves on-prem iSCSI access with local copy of the data, enabling immediate access and low latency; snapshots provide DR to EBS for rapid recovery with minimal changes to existing infrastructure.

question:
A company is hosting a web application from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon Cognito as an identity provider to authenticate users and return a JSON Web Token (JWT) that provides access to protected resources that are stored in another S3 bucket.
Upon deployment of the application, users report errors and are unable to access the protected content. A solutions architect must resolve this issue by providing proper permissions so that users can access the protected content.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.
Update the S3 ACL to allow the application to access the protected content.
Redeploy the application to Amazon S3 to prevent eventually consistent reads in the S3 bucket from affecting the ability of users to access the protected content.
Update the Amazon Cognito pool to use custom attribute mappings within the identity pool and grant users the proper permissions to access the protected content.

explanation:
A) The correct approach is to have the Cognito identity pool assume an IAM role that grants access to the protected S3 resources. This uses temporary credentials issued by Cognito with the necessary permissions, aligning with IAM role-based access for authenticated users.
B) S3 ACLs are not typically used with apps using Cognito/JWT for authorization and do not scale or align with per-user access control via identity pools.
C) S3 eventually consistent reads are unlikely to cause user access errors in this scenario; deployment/read latency is not the root cause.
D) Cognito identity pool custom attribute mappings do not grant access permissions; they map attributes, not authorization policies.

question:
An image hosting company uploads its large assets to Amazon S3 Standard buckets. The company uses multipart upload in parallel by using S3 APIs and overwrites if the same object is uploaded again. For the first 30 days after upload, the objects will be accessed frequently. The objects will be used less frequently after 30 days, but the access patterns for each object will be inconsistent. The company must optimize its S3 storage costs while maintaining high availability and resiliency of stored assets.
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Move assets to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up incomplete multipart uploads.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up expired object delete markers.
Move assets to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
Move assets to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.

explanation: S) A and B are correct because: A) S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access based on usage, preserving high availability and resiliency while optimizing cost for workloads with unpredictable access patterns. B) Lifecycle policy to clean up incomplete multipart uploads reduces wasted storage from abandoned uploads, lowering costs and improving durability by ensuring only complete objects remain. C is incorrect because delete markers relate to versioned buckets and are not about cost optimization for infrequent access. D and E are incorrect because Standard-IA and One Zone-IA require explicit cost considerations and reduced durability options; Intelligent-Tiering better fits mixed and unpredictable access with automated tiering.

question:
A solutions architect must secure a VPC network that hosts Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances contain highly sensitive data and run in a private subnet. According to company policy, the EC2 instances that run in the VPC can access only approved third-party software repositories on the internet for software product updates that use the third party’s URL. Other internet traffic must be blocked.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Update the route table for the private subnet to route the outbound traffic to an AWS Network Firewall firewall. Configure domain list rule groups.
Set up an AWS WAF web ACL. Create a custom set of rules that filter traffic requests based on source and destination IP address range sets.
Implement strict inbound security group rules. Configure an outbound rule that allows traffic only to the authorized software repositories on the internet by specifying the URLs.

Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances. Direct all outbound traffic to the ALB. Use a URL-based rule listener in the ALB’s target group for outbound access to the internet.

explanation:
A) Correct: AWS Network Firewall with domain list rule groups allows you to permit outbound connections only to approved third-party software repositories by blocking all other traffic from private subnets, meeting the “approved URLs only” requirement.
B) Incorrect: AWS WAF protects web traffic at edge or API endpoints; it cannot control arbitrary outbound internet egress from private subnets to specific URLs.
C) Incorrect: Security groups are stateful and cannot filter by URL or enforce outbound rules to specific domains; they rely on IP-based rules, not URL whitelisting.
D) Incorrect: ALB is for inbound traffic distribution; it cannot enforce outbound URL-based egress filtering or control outbound internet access.

question:
A company is hosting a three-tier ecommerce application in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the website on Amazon S3 and integrates the website with an API that handles sales requests. The company hosts the API on three Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The API consists of static and dynamic front-end content along with backend workers that process sales requests asynchronously.
The company is expecting a significant and sudden increase in the number of sales requests during events for the launch of new products.
What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure that all the requests are processed successfully?

choices.text: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Increase the number of EC2 instances to handle the increase in traffic.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on network traffic.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Add an Amazon ElastiCache instance in front of the ALB to reduce traffic for the API to handle.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to receive requests from the website for later processing by the EC2 instances.

explanation:
A) CloudFront for dynamic content and more EC2s: Incorrect because scaling EC2s alone may not smooth spikes in asynchronous processing; dynamic content caching may be less effective, and it ignores decoupling of requests from processing.
B) CloudFront for static content and Auto Scaling: Partial improvement for static assets, but does not address asynchronous processing backlog; lacks decoupling via queuing.
C) CloudFront for dynamic content and ElastiCache in front of ALB: Caching dynamic API responses is complex and may lead to stale data; ElastiCache does not guarantee decoupled, reliable processing backlog.
D) CloudFront for static content and SQS queue: Correct because SQS decouples request ingestion from processing, allowing resilient, scalable handling of asynchronous sales requests; static content delivery via CloudFront reduces origin load.

question:
A security audit reveals that Amazon EC2 instances are not being patched regularly. A solutions architect needs to provide a solution that will run regular security scans across a large fleet of EC2 instances. The solution should also patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule and provide a report of each instance’s patch status.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Set up Amazon Macie to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up a cron job on each EC2 instance to patch the instance on a regular schedule.

Turn on Amazon GuardDuty in the account. Configure GuardDuty to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
Set up Amazon Detective to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.

Turn on Amazon Inspector in the account. Configure Amazon Inspector to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.

explanation: A short, accurate explanation: D is correct because Amazon Inspector provides automated security assessments of EC2 instances for vulnerabilities and exposures, and AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates patching on a defined schedule, with reporting via Inspector findings. A is incorrect because Macie focuses on data discovery, not host vulnerability scanning or patching. B is incorrect because GuardDuty is threat detection, not vulnerability scanning, and Session Manager is a remote command tool, not a patching solution. C is incorrect because Detective analyzes security incidents and relationships, not vulnerability scanning or patch scheduling; EventBridge can trigger actions but lacks integrated patching, so it does not provide a complete patching solution.

question:
A company is planning to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must encrypt the data at rest.
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

choices.text: Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
Create an encryption key. Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager. Use the key to encrypt the DB instances.
Generate a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
Generate a certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.

explanation:
A) Encrypting RDS at rest is achieved by using an AWS KMS key; enabling encryption at creation time or for an existing snapshot/encrypted option ensures data-at-rest protection. AWS KMS manages keys and integrates with RDS.
B) Secrets Manager is for managing credentials and secrets, not for at-rest encryption keys used by RDS. RDS encryption relies on KMS, not stored secrets.
C) ACM certificates enable TLS in transit, not at-rest encryption for RDS data. This is for client-server encryption in transit.
D) IAM certificates are not used for RDS at-rest encryption; SSL/TLS in transit is not configured via IAM certificates.

question:
A company must migrate 20 TB of data from a data center to the AWS Cloud within 30 days. The company’s network bandwidth is limited to 15 Mbps and cannot exceed 70% utilization.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Use AWS Snowball.
Use AWS DataSync.
Use a secure VPN connection.
Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.

explanation: A) AWS Snowball is correct because it provides physical data transfer of large volumes (20 TB) into AWS when network bandwidth is limited, reducing time by shipping a Snowball device rather than transferring over constrained 15 Mbps links. DataSync (B) would still be bound by network bandwidth and may take too long. VPN (C) adds overhead and relies on the same limited link, not suitable for large-scale migration within 30 days. S3 Transfer Acceleration (D) optimizes upload speed from clients over the public internet but still limited by the local wide-area network; it does not address the bulk transfer efficiency as effectively as a physical device for 20 TB.

question:
A company needs to provide its employees with secure access to confidential and sensitive files. The company wants to ensure that the files can be accessed only by authorized users. The files must be downloaded securely to the employees’ devices.
The files are stored in an on-premises Windows file server. However, due to an increase in remote usage, the file server is running out of capacity.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Migrate the file server to an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet. Configure the security group to limit inbound traffic to the employees’ IP addresses.
Migrate the files to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Integrate the Amazon FSx file system with the on-premises Active Directory. Configure AWS Client VPN.
Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a private VPC endpoint. Create a signed URL to allow download.
Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a public VPC endpoint. Allow employees to sign on with AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).

explanation:
Migration to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with AD integration and AWS Client VPN provides secure, authenticated access to Windows-style shares and scalable storage, meeting confidential data access and secure download requirements.
A) Exposes an EC2-based file server in a public subnet; increases risk and still requires on-prem AD integration and VPN/ACLs. Not as scalable or integrated as FSx with AD.
C) S3 with private endpoint and signed URLs lacks native Windows file sharing semantics and persistent SMB access; signed URLs are temporary and not suitable for ongoing authenticated file access.
D) Public VPC endpoint and IAM Identity Center don’t provide Windows file shares or SMB access; public exposure and IAM SSO do not align with on-prem AD integration needs.
B) correctly combines FSx for Windows File Server, AD integration, and AWS Client VPN for secure remote access.

question:
A company’s application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. On the first day of every month at midnight, the application becomes much slower when the month-end financial calculation batch runs. This causes the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances to immediately peak to 100%, which disrupts the application.
What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure the application is able to handle the workload and avoid downtime?

choices.text: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB.
Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization.
Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
Configure Amazon ElastiCache to remove some of the workload from the EC2 instances.

explanation:
The monthly spike can be anticipated; using a scheduled scaling policy aligns capacity with the recurring workload, preventing 100% CPU and ensuring availability across AZs.
A) CloudFront in front of ALB adds caching for static content but does not address a periodic CPU-intensive batch load on EC2 instances.
B) Simple scaling based only on current CPU may react too slowly to a predictable monthly spike and can still cause downtime.
D) ElastiCache helps offload database or cache-heavy work, not the compute-intensive batch processing on EC2 instances.

question:
A company wants to give a customer the ability to use on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to download files that are stored in Amazon S3. The customer’s application uses an SFTP client to download the files.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead and no changes to the customer’s application?

choices.text: Set up AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to synchronize the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
Set up AWS DataSync to synchronize between the on-premises location and the S3 location by using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
Set up a Windows Amazon EC2 instance with SFTP to connect the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Integrate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).

explanation:
AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3 provides native SFTP access to S3 with no changes to the client, and supports Active Directory integration for on-prem credentials, meeting the “no app changes” and least overhead requirements.
A) Correct: SFTP directly to S3 via AWS Transfer Family; integrates with on-prem AD for authentication, minimal manageability.
B) DMS is for database migrations and not designed for file download via SFTP; plus it adds unnecessary data replication complexity.
C) DataSync targets on-prem to S3 sync but does not provide SFTP access or AD-integrated SFTP authentication.
D) EC2-based SFTP requires managing a Windows instance, SFTP server software, and IAM mappings, increasing overhead and maintenance.

question:
A company is experiencing sudden increases in demand. The company needs to provision large Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Machine Image (AMI). The instances will run in an Auto Scaling group. The company needs a solution that provides minimum initialization latency to meet the demand.
Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use the aws ec2 register-image command to create an AMI from a snapshot. Use AWS Step Functions to replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
Enable Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) fast snapshot restore on a snapshot. Provision an AMI by using the snapshot. Replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group with the new AMI.
Enable AMI creation and define lifecycle rules in Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Create an AWS Lambda function that modifies the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke AWS Backup lifecycle policies that provision AMIs. Configure Auto Scaling group capacity limits as an event source in EventBridge.

explanation:
Amazon EBS fast snapshot restore provides low-latency access to recently created AMIs from snapshots, enabling rapid instance provisioning in an Auto Scaling group with minimal initialization time.
A) Using ec2 register-image from a snapshot and Step Functions adds manual orchestration and time to replace ASG AMIs, increasing latency. Not optimal for sudden load.
C) DLM lifecycle with Lambda still requires AMI updates and orchestration; introduces delay and management overhead.
D) EventBridge with Backup policies does not directly optimize AMI provisioning latency or automatic ASG replacement for rapid scale.

question:
A company hosts a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. The company’s IT security guidelines mandate that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days.
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.

Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.

Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.

Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.

explanation:
The correct answer is A. Using Secrets Manager with a KMS key provides encrypted storage, automatic and configurable rotation for the DB credentials, and direct integration with Aurora, minimizing operational overhead. Secrets Manager handles credential rotation in a managed, automated fashion and can be set to a 14-day schedule with correct rotation Lambda hooks if needed.
B is incorrect because rotating passwords via Lambda with Parameter Store requires custom orchestration and lacks built-in rotation for the secrets used by Aurora, increasing operational burden.
C is incorrect due to unnecessary EFS provisioning, file-based credentials, and manual key rotation logic, adding complexity and potential access issues.
D is incorrect because loading credentials from an S3 file and regular downloads introduces latency, risk, and maintenance without native rotation support for database credentials.

question:
A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB instance and five read replicas to support scaling needs. The read replicas must lag no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The database routinely runs scheduled stored procedures.
As traffic on the website increases, the replicas experience additional lag during periods of peak load. A solutions architect must reduce the replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must minimize ongoing operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.

Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.
Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.

Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams.

explanation:
Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas provides built-in replication across replicas with minimal lag, automatic failover, and auto-scaling features. Aurora reduces replication overhead, and Aurora Auto Scaling adjusts read capacity to meet demand while keeping low latency; Aurora also supports MySQL-compatible storage and features, aligning with the stored procedures expressed in the same ecosystem (no need to rewrite to native functions).
B) Redis caching helps read latency but adds caching complexity and potential data staleness; it does not reduce DB replication lag and requires app changes. C) EC2-based MySQL introduces more maintenance and higher operational overhead; lag may persist. D) DynamoDB is a different data model with no stored procedures; migrating and rewriting logic is costly and increases complexity.

question:
A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a high-volume software as a service (SaaS) platform. All data for the platform is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster.
The DR plan must replicate data to a secondary AWS Region.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Use MySQL binary log replication to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Provision one DB instance for the Aurora cluster in the secondary Region.
Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. When setup is complete, remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to continuously replicate data to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. Specify a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region.

explanation:
Aurora Global Database provides low-latency cross-region replication for read/write scalability and automatic replication, meeting DR with minimal ongoing cost by keeping a secondary region synchronized and optional, not a full DR instance unless needed. It is the most cost-effective for continuous DR readiness without ongoing DMS or multiple instances.
A) Binary log replication requires managing replication topology and maintaining a separate DB instance; higher operational cost and complexity.
C) DMS continuous replication adds ongoing replication tasks and compute, increasing cost.
D) Global Database requires at least one secondary instance; option B’s approach implies the same setup with operational efficiency, but DMS/explicit instance removal are unnecessary.

question:
A company has a custom application with embedded credentials that retrieves information from an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. Management says the application must be made more secure with the least amount of programming effort.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create keys. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS. Enable automatic key rotation.

Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function that rotates the credentials in Secret Manager.

Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Secrets Manager.

Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Parameter Store.

explanation: The correct answer is C because Secrets Manager provides automated credential rotation for database users, enabling least-effort rotation without code changes, and applications can retrieve credentials securely from Secrets Manager. A) KMS alone does not store or rotate credentials and loading from KMS is not appropriate for dynamic DB credentials. B) Although Secrets Manager is suitable, rotating credentials inside the application via Lambda adds unnecessary complexity; built-in rotation is preferred. D) Parameter Store can store secrets but supports less robust rotation capabilities for databases than Secrets Manager, making it less ideal for automated DB credential rotation.

question:
A media company hosts its website on AWS. The website application’s architecture includes a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a database that is hosted on Amazon Aurora. The company’s cybersecurity team reports that the application is vulnerable to SQL injection.
How should the company resolve this issue?

choices.text: Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
Create an ALB listener rule to reply to SQL injections with a fixed response.
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
Set up Amazon Inspector to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.

explanation:
A) Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
To mitigate SQL injection, deploy AWS WAF with rules that detect and block common SQLi patterns at the edge before reaching EC2/ALB and Aurora. B is incorrect because ALB rules cannot reliably detect/mitigate SQLi; a fixed response does not adapt to varied payloads. C is incorrect because Shield Advanced protects against DDoS, not SQL injection. D is incorrect because Amazon Inspector is an assessment tool for vulnerabilities on EC2, not real-time web traffic protection. AWS WAF provides targeted, managed protection for SQL injection.

question:
A company has an Amazon S3 data lake that is governed by AWS Lake Formation. The company wants to create a visualization in Amazon QuickSight by joining the data in the data lake with operational data that is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The company wants to enforce column-level authorization so that the company’s marketing team can access only a subset of columns in the database.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Use Amazon EMR to ingest the data directly from the database to the QuickSight SPICE engine. Include only the required columns.

Use AWS Glue Studio to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Attach an IAM policy to the QuickSight users to enforce column-level access control. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.

Use AWS Glue Elastic Views to create a materialized view for the database in Amazon S3. Create an S3 bucket policy to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.

Use a Lake Formation blueprint to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Use Lake Formation to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon Athena as the data source in QuickSight.

explanation:
Lake Formation provides centralized, column-level access control across S3 data stored in the data lake and can enforce permissions for QuickSight via Athena as the data source, meeting the requirement with minimal operational overhead.
A) EMR would require building/integrating a data pipeline and managing SPICE ingestion and column filtering manually, increasing overhead.
B) Glue Studio importing to S3 without built-in column-level authorization tied to Lake Formation lacks governance for per-column access in QuickSight; IAM policies alone cannot enforce column-level data masking at query time.
C) Glue Elastic Views creates a materialized view in S3 but does not offer Lake Formation–driven per-column access control for QuickSight; separate policies would be needed.
D) Correct: Lake Formation blueprint ingests into S3 and enforces column-level access for QuickSight via Athena, aligning with governance and minimal ops.

question:
A transaction processing company has weekly scripted batch jobs that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The number of transactions can vary, but the baseline CPU utilization that is noted on each run is at least 60%. The company needs to provision the capacity 30 minutes before the jobs run.
Currently, engineers complete this task by manually modifying the Auto Scaling group parameters. The company does not have the resources to analyze the required capacity trends for the Auto Scaling group counts. The company needs an automated way to modify the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Create a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on the CPU utilization metric. Set the target value for the metric to 60%.

Create a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Set the appropriate desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity. Set the recurrence to weekly. Set the start time to 30 minutes before the batch jobs run.

Create a predictive scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on forecast. Set the scaling metric to CPU utilization. Set the target value for the metric to 60%. In the policy, set the instances to pre-launch 30 minutes before the jobs run.

Create an Amazon EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the CPU utilization metric value for the Auto Scaling group reaches 60%. Configure the Lambda function to increase the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity and maximum capacity by 20%.

explanation: The correct answer is C because predictive scaling uses forecasted demand to pre-provision capacity, allowing 30 minutes lead time before batch jobs and reducing manual intervention; it pre-launches instances to meet anticipated CPU utilization, aligning with least operational overhead. A) Dynamic scaling reacts to current load only and cannot guarantee 30-minute pre-provisioning. B) Scheduled scaling requires fixed times but lacks adaptation to actual demand and accurate forecasting. D) EventBridge/Lambda reacts after the metric hits threshold, causing reactive rather than proactive scaling and adds operational steps. C leverages forecast-based pre-provisioning with minimal ongoing management.

question:
A solutions architect is designing a company’s disaster recovery (DR) architecture. The company has a MySQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet with scheduled backup. The DR design needs to include multiple AWS Regions.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Migrate the MySQL database to multiple EC2 instances. Configure a standby EC2 instance in the DR Region. Turn on replication.
Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS. Use a Multi-AZ deployment. Turn on read replication for the primary DB instance in the different Availability Zones.
Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon Aurora global database. Host the primary DB cluster in the primary Region. Host the secondary DB cluster in the DR Region.
Store the scheduled backup of the MySQL database in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use the data backup to restore the database in the DR Region.

explanation:
The correct answer (C) uses Amazon Aurora Global Database to provide cross-region disaster recovery with low operational overhead. It replicates committed data to a secondary region with low RPO/LRO and automatic failover capabilities, while remaining a managed service with minimal manual intervention.
A) Involving multiple EC2 instances requires manual replication setup and failover orchestration; higher operational overhead.
B) RDS Multi-AZ with read replication in different AZs does not provide cross-region DR and involves manual promotion in a DR scenario.
D) S3 CRR stores backups but requires a restore process; this is a backup-first approach with higher recovery work and latency.

question:
A company has a Java application that uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to parse messages. The application cannot parse messages that are larger than 256 KB in size. The company wants to implement a solution to give the application the ability to parse messages as large as 50 MB.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?

choices.text: Use the Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java to host messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon S3.
Use Amazon EventBridge to post large messages from the application instead of Amazon SQS.
Change the limit in Amazon SQS to handle messages that are larger than 256 KB.
Store messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Configure Amazon SQS to reference this location in the messages.

explanation:
The correct answer is A. The SQS Extended Client Library for Java stores large message payloads in S3 and keeps a pointer in SQS, allowing the application to process messages up to 50 MB with minimal code changes.
B is incorrect because EventBridge is not designed to replace SQS for message payloads and would require substantial redesign and integration changes.
C is incorrect because SQS has fixed limits; the limit cannot be raised to 50 MB.
D is incorrect because SQS does not natively reference EFS; integrating would be more complex and require custom tooling.

question:
A company wants to restrict access to the content of one of its main web applications and to protect the content by using authorization techniques available on AWS. The company wants to implement a serverless architecture and an authentication solution for fewer than 100 users. The solution needs to integrate with the main web application and serve web content globally. The solution must also scale as the company's user base grows while providing the lowest login latency possible.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.

explanation:
C) A) is correct.
A) Using Amazon Cognito for authentication provides scalable, serverless user pools for up to 100 users with easy federation and app integration. Lambda@Edge enables authorization logic at CloudFront edge locations for low-latency access, and CloudFront serves content globally with caching and edge rules, making it cost-effective and scalable for a global web app.
B) Directory Service tied to Active Directory is heavier, not serverless, and ALB is not ideal for global static content delivery at edge. Lambda alone would not provide global edge authorization.
C) S3 Transfer Acceleration is for faster uploads/downloads, not suitable for dynamic authorization at edge; lacks identity management.
D) Directory Service plus Lambda@Edge adds complexity and Elastic Beanstalk is not the lowest-latency serverless option for global web serving.

question:
A company has an aging network-attached storage (NAS) array in its data center. The NAS array presents SMB shares and NFS shares to client workstations. The company does not want to purchase a new NAS array. The company also does not want to incur the cost of renewing the NAS array’s support contract. Some of the data is accessed frequently, but much of the data is inactive.
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that migrates the data to Amazon S3, uses S3 Lifecycle policies, and maintains the same look and feel for the client workstations. The solutions architect has identified AWS Storage Gateway as part of the solution.
Which type of storage gateway should the solutions architect provision to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Volume Gateway
Tape Gateway
Amazon FSx File Gateway
Amazon S3 File Gateway

explanation:
Storage Gateway should present a local NAS-like interface backed by S3, enabling SMB/NFS access while migrating to S3 with lifecycle policies; File Gateway provides file-based access to S3 and is designed for on-prem hosts to access S3 as a file share.
A) Volume Gateway is block-based iSCSI storage, not suitable for SMB/NFS via a familiar file share.
B) Tape Gateway emulates tape libraries for archival, not active file shares.
C) Amazon FSx File Gateway is not a defined gateway service; FSx offers managed file systems, not a gateway to S3.
D) Amazon S3 File Gateway provides SMB/NFS-compatible file shares backed by S3, supporting data tiering and lifecycle policies.

question:
A company has an application that is running on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect has standardized the company on a particular instance family and various instance sizes based on the current needs of the company.
The company wants to maximize cost savings for the application over the next 3 years. The company needs to be able to change the instance family and sizes in the next 6 months based on application popularity and usage.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Compute Savings Plan
EC2 Instance Savings Plan
Zonal Reserved Instances
Standard Reserved Instances

explanation:
The correct answer is A) Compute Savings Plan.
Compute Savings Plans offer the broadest flexibility, committing to compute usage (measured in $/hour) across any instance family, size, region, or Sagemaker/Lambda usage, with the ability to switch instance families as needs change over the 3-year term, maximizing overall savings.
B) EC2 Instance Savings Plan is narrower: applies only to a specific instance family within a chosen region, limiting flexibility to switch families.
C) Zonal Reserved Instances require payment upfront/partial and apply to a single Availability Zone, restricting changes and topologies.
D) Standard Reserved Instances are fixed to a specific instance type in a region, with limited flexibility for changing families or sizes during the term.

question:
A company collects data from a large number of participants who use wearable devices. The company stores the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table and uses applications to analyze the data. The data workload is constant and predictable. The company wants to stay at or below its forecasted budget for DynamoDB.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Use provisioned mode and DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA). Reserve capacity for the forecasted workload.
Use provisioned mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs).
Use on-demand mode. Set the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) high enough to accommodate changes in the workload.
Use on-demand mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) with reserved capacity.

explanation:
Provisioned mode with explicit RCUs and WCUs aligns capacity exactly to forecasted workload, enabling predictable costs within budget and avoiding pay-per-request variability. This is cost-effective for a constant, predictable workload.
A) Incorrect: DynamoDB Standard-IA is not a valid capacity model for DynamoDB tables; there is no Standard-IA in DynamoDB. B) Correct: Provisioned mode with specified RCUs/WCUs gives predictable costs and supports reserved capacity optimization if applicable. C) Incorrect: On-demand mode charges per request and is less cost-predictable for steady workloads. D) Incorrect: On-demand with reserved capacity is not a valid configuration; reserved capacity applies to provisioned mode, not on-demand.

question:
A company stores confidential data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database in the ap-southeast-3 Region. The database is encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The company was recently acquired and must securely share a backup of the database with the acquiring company’s AWS account in ap-southeast-3.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Create a database snapshot. Copy the snapshot to a new unencrypted snapshot. Share the new snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
Create a database snapshot. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key policy. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
Create a database snapshot that uses a different AWS managed KMS key. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key alias. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
Create a database snapshot. Download the database snapshot. Upload the database snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the acquiring company’s AWS account.

explanation:
The correct answer is B.
A) Incorrect: Copying to an unencrypted snapshot defeats encryption and compliance requirements; the data remains sensitive and not protected as in the original KMS-managed state.
C) Incorrect: Changing to a different AWS managed KMS key and alias does not grant cross-account access to the original customer-managed key; sharing requires key policy updates, not a key alias switch.
D) Incorrect: Downloading and re-uploading to S3 introduces additional risk, and KMS encryption is not preserved or automatically aligned with cross-account access; this is not the proper method for sharing an RDS/Aurora snapshot.
B) Correct: Include the acquiring account in the KMS key policy so they can decrypt the snapshot, preserving encryption and meeting access control.

question:
A company uses a 100 GB Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server Single-AZ DB instance in the us-east-1 Region to store customer transactions. The company needs high availability and automatic recovery for the DB instance.
The company must also run reports on the RDS database several times a year. The report process causes transactions to take longer than usual to post to the customers’ accounts. The company needs a solution that will improve the performance of the report process.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Modify the DB instance from a Single-AZ DB instance to a Multi-AZ deployment.
Take a snapshot of the current DB instance. Restore the snapshot to a new RDS deployment in another Availability Zone.
Create a read replica of the DB instance in a different Availability Zone. Point all requests for reports to the read replica.
Migrate the database to RDS Custom.
Use RDS Proxy to limit reporting requests to the maintenance window.

explanation:
High availability and automatic recovery are provided by Multi-AZ (A), and read replicas (C) offload long-running reporting queries, improving performance without affecting the primary write workload.
A) Correct. Converting to Multi-AZ enables automatic failover and standby synchronization, meeting HA and recovery needs.
B) Incorrect. Snapshots/restores are manual DR steps, not automatic HA, and don’t provide an active read path for reports.
C) Correct. A read replica in another AZ offloads report queries from the primary, improving report performance without impacting transactional throughput.
D) Incorrect. RDS Custom is for different management models and is not needed for standard HA + read-scaling; it’s not the solution here.
E) Incorrect. RDS Proxy optimizes connections but does not specifically ensure HA or offload reporting workloads in this scenario.

question:
A company is moving its data management application to AWS. The company wants to transition to an event-driven architecture. The architecture needs to be more distributed and to use serverless concepts while performing the different aspects of the workflow. The company also wants to minimize operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Build out the workflow in AWS Glue. Use AWS Glue to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.
Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Step Functions to invoke the workflow steps on the EC2 instances.
Build out the workflow in Amazon EventBridge. Use EventBridge to invoke AWS Lambda functions on a schedule to process the workflow steps.
Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Use Step Functions to create a state machine. Use the state machine to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.

explanation:
D) Step Functions provides a serverless, fully managed workflow engine with a state machine to coordinate Lambda functions, enabling a distributed, event-driven architecture with minimal operational overhead.
A) AWS Glue is ETL-focused and not designed for general workflow orchestration with lightweight Lambda-based steps; it adds unnecessary complexity.
B) Using EC2 defeats serverless and increases operational burden; Step Functions with Lambda is the recommended serverless orchestration pattern.
C) EventBridge can trigger Lambdas but lacks the built-in state machine orchestration and fault-tolerant workflow management that Step Functions provides.

question:
A company is designing the network for an online multi-player game. The game uses the UDP networking protocol and will be deployed in eight AWS Regions. The network architecture needs to minimize latency and packet loss to give end users a high-quality gaming experience.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Setup a transit gateway in each Region. Create inter-Region peering attachments between each transit gateway.
Set up AWS Global Accelerator with UDP listeners and endpoint groups in each Region.
Set up Amazon CloudFront with UDP turned on. Configure an origin in each Region.
Set up a VPC peering mesh between each Region. Turn on UDP for each VPC.

explanation:
Global Accelerator with UDP listeners and regional endpoint groups minimizes latency and loss by routing user traffic to optimal regional endpoints and providing fixed-entry points, which is ideal for latency-sensitive UDP gaming across eight Regions.
A) Transit gateways and inter-Region peering do not provide global any-to-any optimized routing or health-based failover; adds complexity and higher latency paths.
C) CloudFront is a CDN for HTTP/HTTPS; UDP support and game-state real-time traffic are not suited, and CloudFront origins in multiple Regions don’t optimize per-user routing for UDP gaming.
D) VPC peering mesh across Regions lacks global any-to-many routing, centralized health checks, and performance optimization for UDP traffic.

question:
A company hosts a three-tier web application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. The web application uses a self-managed MySQL database that is hosted on an EC2 instance to store data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. The MySQL database currently uses a 1 TB Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volume. The company expects traffic of 1,000 IOPS for both reads and writes at peak traffic.
The company wants to minimize any disruptions, stabilize performance, and reduce costs while retaining the capacity for double the IOPS. The company wants to move the database tier to a fully managed solution that is highly available and fault tolerant.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.text: Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with an io2 Block Express EBS volume.
Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with a General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume.
Use Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tiers.
Use two large EC2 instances to host the database in active-passive mode.

explanation:
The correct option is B.
A) Incorrect: io2 Block Express in RDS would increase cost; Multi-AZ with io2 is not the most cost-effective for MySQL, and the requirement is fault tolerance and managed service with lower cost.
B) Correct: Multi-AZ RDS for MySQL with gp2 provides managed, highly available DB with automated backups and failover, at a lower cost than io2, and gp2 suffices for ~1000 IOPS with burst balance; meets high availability and maintenance needs.
C) Incorrect: S3 Intelligent-Tiering does not provide a relational database or in-place transactional capabilities; not suitable for a live DB.
D) Incorrect: Two large EC2s in active-passive increases management overhead and cost; lacks managed RDS benefits.

question:
A company hosts a serverless application on AWS. The application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The company notices an increase in application errors that result from database connection timeouts during times of peak traffic or unpredictable traffic. The company needs a solution that reduces the application failures with the least amount of change to the code.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Reduce the Lambda concurrency rate.
Enable RDS Proxy on the RDS DB instance.
Resize the RDS DB instance class to accept more connections.
Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand scaling.

explanation:
A) Enable RDS Proxy on the RDS DB instance
B) Reason: RDS Proxy pools and manages database connections for Lambda, reducing connection timeouts during burst traffic with minimal code changes. It scales connections efficiently and handles idle connections, improving application reliability.
C) Reducing Lambda concurrency or sizing DB instance alone doesn’t address connection burst handling or idle connection storms; it may still gridlock under peak traffic.
D) Migrating to DynamoDB involves a major architectural change and data model shifts; not a least-change solution for a relational workload.

question:
A company is migrating an old application to AWS. The application runs a batch job every hour and is CPU intensive. The batch job takes 15 minutes on average with an on-premises server. The server has 64 virtual CPU (vCPU) and 512 GiB of memory.
Which solution will run the batch job within 15 minutes with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Use AWS Lambda with functional scaling.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate.
Use Amazon Lightsail with AWS Auto Scaling.
Use AWS Batch on Amazon EC2.

explanation:
Using AWS Batch on EC2 provides scalable compute resources with managed job queues and scheduling, enabling a 15-minute turnaround for a CPU-intensive, hourly batch workload with minimal operational overhead.
A) Lambda is unsuitable for 15-minute CPU-intensive batch due to 15-minute execution limit and potential concurrency management overhead.
B) ECS with Fargate adds orchestration but may introduce higher per-task cost and tighter resource limits for long-running, CPU-heavy jobs.
C) Lightsail lacks sufficient batch orchestration, scaling, and integration for large-scale, hourly jobs with minimal ops.
D) AWS Batch on EC2 offers job queues, compute environments, and automatic scaling tuned to CPU-intensive workloads with low admin effort.

question:
A company stores its data objects in Amazon S3 Standard storage. A solutions architect has found that 75% of the data is rarely accessed after 30 days. The company needs all the data to remain immediately accessible with the same high availability and resiliency, but the company wants to minimize storage costs.
Which storage solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Move the data objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
Move the data objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately.

explanation:
Moving to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days preserves immediate access, high availability, and durability while reducing storage costs for rarely accessed data.
A) S3 Glacier Deep Archive is designed for long-term archival with retrieval delays; not immediate access.
B) S3 Standard-IA retains high durability and access predictability with lower cost for infrequently accessed data, after a 30-day window.
C) S3 One Zone-IA offers lower durability (single AZ) and is not ideal for data requiring the same high availability and resiliency.
D) Moving immediately to One Zone-IA would reduce durability and availability risk from the start.

question:
A gaming company is moving its public scoreboard from a data center to the AWS Cloud. The company uses Amazon EC2 Windows Server instances behind an Application Load Balancer to host its dynamic application. The company needs a highly available storage solution for the application. The application consists of static files and dynamic server-side code.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront to cache objects at the edge.
Store the static files on Amazon S3. Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache objects at the edge.
Store the server-side code on Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.
Store the server-side code on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the FSx for Windows File Server volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.
Store the server-side code on a General Purpose SSD (gp2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on each EC2 instance to share the files.

explanation:
A) Correct: Static files on S3 with CloudFront provides durable, highly available object storage with edge caching to reduce latency for a global audience. D) Correct: FSx for Windows File Server offers shared file storage accessible from multiple EC2 Windows instances, suitable for server-side code that needs a shared filesystem.
B) Incorrect: ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service for apps, not edge storage for static files.
C) Incorrect: EFS is shared Linux-based NFS; not ideal for Windows Server apps as a primary shared filesystem in this context.
E) Incorrect: Mounting a single EBS volume on multiple EC2 instances isn’t supported; EBS is instance-store specific and lacks built-in multi-attach for Windows in this scenario.

question:
A social media company runs its application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The application has more than a billion images stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and processes thousands of images each second. The company wants to resize the images dynamically and serve appropriate formats to clients.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Install an external image management library on an EC2 instance. Use the image management library to process the images.
Create a CloudFront origin request policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.
Use a Lambda@Edge function with an external image management library. Associate the Lambda@Edge function with the CloudFront behaviors that serve the images.
Create a CloudFront response headers policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.

explanation:
Lambda@Edge can run code at CloudFront edge locations to resize images and convert formats on-the-fly, minimizing latency and operational overhead. It leverages a function with an image processing library and executes during requests, scaling automatically with traffic.
A) Requires managing and scaling EC2 instances and the library, increasing operational overhead.
B) Origin request policy controls headers, not image processing; it cannot perform resizing.
D) Response headers policy only affects headers, not image transformation or resizing.
C) Uses serverless edge compute close to users, handles dynamic resizing and format adaptation with minimal upkeep.

question:
A hospital needs to store patient records in an Amazon S3 bucket. The hospital’s compliance team must ensure that all protected health information (PHI) is encrypted in transit and at rest. The compliance team must administer the encryption key for data at rest.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Create a public SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Associate the certificate with Amazon S3. Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.

Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Assign the compliance team to manage the SSE-S3 keys.

Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.

Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Use Amazon Macie to protect the sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3. Assign the compliance team to manage Macie.

explanation:
A) Incorrect: SSL cert in ACM attached to S3 is not a direct mechanism for S3 encryption at rest; SSE-KMS with compliant key management is required for PHI at rest.
B) Incorrect: SSE-S3 does not use customer-managed KMS keys; PHI compliance requires customer-managed keys (KMS) and access control by the compliance team.
C) Correct: Enforces encrypted transport via aws:SecureTransport, uses SSE-KMS for at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys, and grants key management to the compliance team, meeting HIPAA-like requirements.
D) Incorrect: Macie provides data discovery and classification, not encryption at rest or key management; fails PHI-at-rest and key-management requirements.

question:
A company uses Amazon API Gateway to run a private gateway with two REST APIs in the same VPC. The BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service to ensure that enough funds are available before a stock can be purchased. The company has noticed in the VPC flow logs that the BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service over the internet instead of through the VPC. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the APIs communicate through the VPC.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?

choices.text: Add an X-API-Key header in the HTTP header for authorization.
Use an interface endpoint.
Use a gateway endpoint.
Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue between the two REST APIs.

explanation:
The correct answer is B. Use an interface endpoint. This creates an elastic network interface in the VPC to enable private connectivity to the API Gateway REST APIs, ensuring that calls between BuyStock and CheckFunds stay inside the VPC without internet traversal and with minimal code changes.
A) Adding an X-API-Key does not affect network routing; it only provides API access control, not private VPC connectivity.
C) A gateway endpoint supports S3 and DynamoDB, not API Gateway private endpoints for REST APIs.
D) SQS introduces asynchronous messaging, adding complexity and latency rather than ensuring in-VPC API calls.

question:
A company hosts a multiplayer gaming application on AWS. The company wants the application to read data with sub-millisecond latency and run one-time queries on historical data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Use Amazon RDS for data that is frequently accessed. Run a periodic custom script to export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.

Store the data directly in an Amazon S3 bucket. Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy to move older data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term storage. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.

Use Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for data that is frequently accessed. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using DynamoDB table export. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.

Use Amazon DynamoDB for data that is frequently accessed. Turn on streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read the data from Kinesis Data Streams. Store the records in an Amazon S3 bucket.

explanation:
D) Use Amazon DynamoDB for data that is frequently accessed. Turn on streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read the data from Kinesis Data Streams. Store the records in an Amazon S3 bucket.
A) RDS with periodic export adds latency and operational steps; not sub-millisecond for gaming read latency.
B) S3 with Athena provides only batch/query-based access, not sub-ms latency for hot data; Glacier Deep Archive is for long-term, not hot workloads.
C) DynamoDB with DAX provides microsecond, cache-backed reads for hot data; DynamoDB export to S3 enables analytics with Athena, minimizing ops.
D) Firehose/Streams path adds complexity and may not meet sub-millisecond reads for active data.

question:
A company uses a payment processing system that requires messages for a particular payment ID to be received in the same order that they were sent. Otherwise, the payments might be processed incorrectly.
Which actions should a solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Write the messages to an Amazon DynamoDB table with the payment ID as the partition key.
Write the messages to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with the payment ID as the partition key.
Write the messages to an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster with the payment ID as the key.
Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Set the message attribute to use the payment I
Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Set the message group to use the payment ID.

explanation:
A concise explanation: Using a Kinesis data stream with the payment ID as the partition key ensures ordered processing per partition, and an SQS FIFO queue with the payment ID as the message group ensures strict per-group ordering. Together, they guarantee that all messages for a given payment ID are delivered in order.
A) DynamoDB with payment ID as partition key does not provide inherent message ordering guarantees for stream processing.
C) ElastiCache Memcached is a cache, not a durable ordered messaging service.
D) SQS standard queue does not guarantee ordering across messages.
E) SQS FIFO queue with the payment ID as the message group ensures per-group in-order delivery.

question:
A company is building a game system that needs to send unique events to separate leaderboard, matchmaking, and authentication services concurrently. The company needs an AWS event-driven system that guarantees the order of the events.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.text: Amazon EventBridge event bus
Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topics
Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topics
Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues

explanation: Event-driven with strict per-event ordering and separate destinations is provided by SNS FIFO topics, ensuring ordered delivery and deduplication across multiple subscribers, suitable for concurrent services (leaderboard, matchmaking, authentication) that need same-order events. A) EventBridge supports event routing but not guaranteed per-event ordering across multiple targets. C) SNS standard topics do not guarantee ordering. D) SQS FIFO queues guarantee ordering per queue but do not natively publish to multiple distinct services simultaneously from a single source without additional fan-out; SNS FIFO is designed for fan-out to multiple endpoints with ordering. Therefore B is correct.

question:
A hospital is designing a new application that gathers symptoms from patients. The hospital has decided to use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) and Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) in the architecture.
A solutions architect is reviewing the infrastructure design. Data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Only authorized personnel of the hospital should be able to access the data.
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.
Turn on server-side encryption on the SNS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply a key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.

Turn on encryption on the SNS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals. Set a condition in the topic policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.

Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply a key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals. Set a condition in the queue policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.

Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply an IAM policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals. Set a condition in the queue policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.

explanation:
Satisfying data at rest with SQS/SNS encryption using AWS KMS customer-managed keys and enforcing access with strict key policies plus transport security across SQS queues.
A) Incorrect: SQS server-side encryption exists, but requires proper KMS key policy and access controls; statement about “default key policy” is insufficient alone and ignores TLS enforcement for in-transit protection on queues.
B) Correct: SNS encryption with a KMS CMK and a restrictive key policy ensures at-rest protection and authorized access.
C) Incorrect: SNS supports encryption at rest; adding a topic policy TLS condition is not applicable to in-transit SNS-to-endpoint; TLS for client connections is not enforced via this policy construct.
D) Correct: SQS SSE with a CMK and restrictive key policy, plus a queue policy condition enforcing TLS, covers both at-rest encryption and only encrypted transit access.
E) Incorrect: IAM policy alone for key usage is not the correct mechanism; key policy (not IAM policy) governs KMS key access; TLS condition on queue policy should be used.

question:
A company runs a web application that is backed by Amazon RDS. A new database administrator caused data loss by accidentally editing information in a database table. To help recover from this type of incident, the company wants the ability to restore the database to its state from 5 minutes before any change within the last 30 days.
Which feature should the solutions architect include in the design to meet this requirement?

choices.text: Read replicas
Manual snapshots
Automated backups
Multi-AZ deployments

explanation:
Automated backups provide point-in-time recovery for Amazon RDS, enabling restore to any second within a retention period (up to 35 days). The requirement to revert to 5 minutes before any change within the last 30 days is satisfied by automated backups with a suitable backup retention window and, if needed, transaction logs for PITR.
A) Read replicas do not support point-in-time restore of the primary; they are for offloading reads and eventual data consistency, not recovery from accidental edits.
B) Manual snapshots are static and must be created ahead of time; they do not cover continuous 30-day PITR automatically.
D) Multi-AZ improves availability and durability but not PITR restore to a specific prior moment.

question:
A company’s web application consists of an Amazon API Gateway API in front of an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB database. The Lambda function handles the business logic, and the DynamoDB table hosts the data. The application uses Amazon Cognito user pools to identify the individual users of the application. A solutions architect needs to update the application so that only users who have a subscription can access premium content.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.text: Enable API caching and throttling on the API Gateway API.
Set up AWS WAF on the API Gateway API. Create a rule to filter users who have a subscription.
Apply fine-grained IAM permissions to the premium content in the DynamoDB table.
Implement API usage plans and API keys to limit the access of users who do not have a subscription.

explanation:
Implement API usage plans and API keys to control access based on subscription status with minimal operational overhead.
A) Incorrect. API caching/throttling do not enforce subscription-based access; they optimize performance rather than authorize users.
B) Incorrect. WAF rules require custom integrations and ongoing maintenance for per-user subscription checks; not a scalable or low-overhead solution for individual user authorization.
C) Incorrect. Fine-grained IAM permissions apply to principals within AWS, not to end users authenticated via Cognito in a web app; DynamoDB-level restrictions won’t map cleanly to per-user app access without additional auth logic.
D) Correct. API Gateway usage plans and API keys provide per-user access control aligned with subscription status, without modifying Lambda or DynamoDB logic, offering low operational overhead.

question:
A company is using Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to its UDP-based application for users around the world. The application is hosted on redundant servers in the company's on-premises data centers in the United States, Asia, and Europe. The company’s compliance requirements state that the application must be hosted on premises. The company wants to improve the performance and availability of the application.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.text: Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the NLBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.

Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the ALBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.

Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three NLBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.

Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three ALBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.

explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator provides a single, global anycast entry point with health checks and fast failover to regional endpoints, optimizing latency for UDP traffic and enabling on-premises endpoints behind AWS resources. Using three NLBs in AWS Regions as endpoints leverages NLBs’ UDP support and preserves on-premises hosting while Global Accelerator handles global routing and health. A CNAME to the accelerator DNS exposes a single, resilient address.
A) Correct: uses NLBs in regions with Global Accelerator for UDP traffic to on-prem endpoints.
